claim: normalize_identifiers and traverse_scope run only when a statement has a non-exempt star, and any unexpected exception from them is logged at WARNING with a traceback and refuses the query with a message naming only the exception type.
source_excerpt: `normalize_identifiers` and `traverse_scope` run only when the statement has a star that is not exempt, so a query without one never depends on them. Any unexpected exception from them is logged at `WARNING` with a traceback and refuses the query (`whole-row select check errored (<exception type>)`), as the read-only guard fails closed. The exception text stays in the log, out of the error the model and user see, because scope analysis can quote a table or schema name.

claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: The new test file never exercises the guard's one fail-open lever against a query that also carries a real table star. `_is_exempt` in `src/sqllens/safety/whole_row.py` (lines 155-160) exempts a star whose parent chain reaches `exp.Count`, and any star with an `exp.Exists` ancestor. The refused-shape table in `tests/unit/test_safety_whole_row.py` (lines 51-99) contains no query that combines an outer whole-row star with one of those constructs — no `SELECT * FROM users WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = users.id)`, and no `SELECT COUNT(*), u.* FROM users u GROUP BY ...`. The allowed-shape entries only put stars *inside* `EXISTS`. The code at this head is correct, because the lookup is `star.find_ancestor`. A later change that widened the exemption from an ancestor test to a per-statement test, or that exempted a whole `SELECT` containing a `Count`, would let `SELECT *` over a people table through — the exact leak this change exists to close — with the whole suite still green. (raised by 1/6 agents)
